_comment: Cool-white LED: the lit, diffused face of an LED strip, panel or cove light at about 6500 K. Emissive: its defining observable is that it glows, a neutral-to-cool white. The emissive colour is the article's, not a Creator port (LCDSchema), so a white strip is its own article and cannot be reached by tinting Neon_Signage or LED_WarmWhite. The matter under the glow is the milky polycarbonate diffuser (its colour and gloss show only where the glow is dimmed). Param-only. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), fingerprints, gated by the Grime mask; the master's emission is a constant the layers do not reach, so wear shows only on the diffuser's reflection, not in the glow. The sibling of LED_WarmWhite, same diffuser and same luminance. Built for the platform's generated architectural Set (261004_R_PlatformSetMaterialAsks.md, A2).
name: LED_CoolWhite_Clean_Base_s01_v01

sources.note: Only specular_ior is taken, for the polycarbonate diffuser: the entry is the clear resin, not a milky diffuser.

sources.why: emission_color 0.993, 0.992, 1.0 is the centre of the 6500 K cool-white LED chromaticity bin (CIE xy 0.3123, 0.3282, a hair bluer than D65) in linear sRGB, scaled so the largest channel is 1. A 6500 K blackbody was not used: it sits below the daylight locus and reads faintly pink (1.0, 0.944, 0.993). emission_luminance 12 matches the library's other emitters (Neon_Signage, LED_WarmWhite) on the rig's relative scale, not measured nits: where a lit white surface renders near 1.0, the strip is about 3.6 stops over it. The diffuser under it is the milky polycarbonate of LED_WarmWhite (base 0.80, 0.80, 0.78, roughness 0.3). Physically Based's materials list has no LED or light entry.
